amendments.because: Owner: use Fast mode for quick work too
amendments.done_when: Codex runs through the app server use the model's Fast tier for an item that other planned work waits on and for repair rounds after the first, and run normally otherwise or when the model has no Fast tier; one forge.toml setting turns Fast off or always on; forge doctor shows which applies, and upgrading tells existing repos in one line that Fast is now on when it matters. New and existing client repos get it on init or upgrade plus sync, and a test covers both.

done_when: Codex runs through the app server use the model's Fast tier for quick work (every fix, every repair round after the first) and for an item that other planned work waits on, and run normally otherwise or when the model has no Fast tier; one forge.toml setting turns Fast off or always on; forge doctor shows which applies, and upgrading tells existing repos in one line that Fast is now on for quick work. New and existing client repos get it on init or upgrade plus sync, and a test covers both.

findings.body: Raise: Scale. In the default `needed` mode, every first-round task that is neither a fix nor already in a repair round calls `board.machine_board()` before Codex starts. That builds the full board, reads the repository's item history, and makes GitHub requests for open and merged pull requests, including uncached `gh pr list --limit 1000` calls (`src/forge/board.py:231,241,246-251`; `src/forge/nextstep.py:670-675`). In a normal repo with many completed items and pull requests, each new independent task pays this unrelated local and network cost even though it will run at normal speed.
findings.title: Full board scan delays every ordinary first Codex work turn

why: Codex offers a Fast mode at about twice the speed and Forge never uses it
